title_en: Fall 2026 Graduate Module Master's/Doctoral Seminar Auditing Application
summary: New graduate students and integrated master's-doctoral program students entering the doctoral stage must apply to audit the Master's/Doctoral Seminar course offered by their own module in Fall 2026. Apply by email to the teaching assistant of the chosen course (listed in Attachment 2) by Wednesday, 12 August 2026. Do not formally register for the course during the course registration period, because the first semester is auditing only.
applies_to: Graduate students starting the first (auditing) semester of the module Master's/Doctoral Seminar in Fall 2026: new graduate students admitted for the second half of the 2026 academic year (Master's Seminar), and integrated master's-doctoral program students entering the doctoral stage (Doctoral Seminar, normally in their 4th semester). The seminar is a mandatory requirement for completing the master's and doctoral programs.

dates.what: Deadline to apply by email to audit the Master's/Doctoral Seminar
English presentation skills seminar, online via Zoom (optional for auditing students; details to be announced later)

conditions: The module Master's/Doctoral Seminar is a mandatory requirement for completing the master's and doctoral programs and must be taken before completion.
The seminar runs over two semesters: the first semester is auditing without course registration, and the second semester requires course registration and an English presentation to earn 3 credits.
Integrated master's-doctoral program students must complete both the Master's Seminar and the Doctoral Seminar (based on entering the doctoral stage in the 4th semester).
Do not formally register for the seminar course during the course registration period in the first (auditing) semester.
Courses with the same name other than the 16 courses listed in Attachment 2 are counted as general graduate courses, not the mandatory seminar (their subtitle code and subtitle name differ).
You must apply to audit a course offered by your own module (your academic advisor's module).
Exception: for the Master's Seminar in the Semiconductor and Computer modules, you may apply to audit the course that matches your presentation topic.
The English presentation skills seminar is not mandatory for auditing students; only those who wish may apply, and attendance is recommended in the registration semester.
steps: Fall 2026 new students: read Attachment 1 (Fall 2026 Mandatory Graduate Seminar Auditing Guide for New Students) carefully; its content was not read for this translation.
Check Attachment 2 to find the seminar course offered by your module and the email address of its teaching assistant (the attachment content was not read for this translation).
By Wednesday, 12 August 2026, email the teaching assistant of the chosen course with your student ID, name, academic advisor, email address and mobile phone number.
During the course registration period, do not formally register for the seminar course.
Optionally, watch for a later notice and apply for the English presentation skills seminar (4 September 2026, 2:00–3:00 p.m., Zoom).
In the following semester, register for the seminar and give your English presentation to earn 3 credits.
For questions, contact the department office, Building 301, Room 319; contact details are in the original notice.
translation:
Fall 2026 Graduate Module 'Master's/Doctoral Seminar' (석박세미나) Course Auditing (청강) Guide (New Students / Integrated Program Students Entering the Doctoral Stage)

We announce the application for auditing the graduate module 'Master's/Doctoral Seminar' courses for the second semester of 2026.

New graduate students admitted for the second half of the 2026 academic year must check the content of [Attachment 1] so that there are no mistakes in their auditing application.

1. Overview of the Graduate Module 'Master's/Doctoral Seminar'
- It is a mandatory requirement for completing the master's and doctoral programs. Master's and doctoral seminars for each module are offered every semester, and you must take the seminar of your own module before completion.
- It runs over two semesters: the first semester is conducted as auditing without course registration, and in the second semester you earn 3 credits through course registration and an English presentation.
- Integrated master's-doctoral program students must complete both the 'Master's Seminar' and the 'Doctoral Seminar' (based on entering the doctoral stage in the 4th semester).
 · Master's Seminar: audit in the 1st semester → register and present in the 2nd semester (3 credits)
 · Doctoral Seminar: audit in the 4th semester → register and present in the 5th semester (3 credits)
 ※ In the first semester (1st semester, 4th semester), you do not formally register for the course; it is conducted as auditing only.

2. Auditing Application
- Deadline: by Wednesday, 12 August 2026
- How to apply: by email to the teaching assistant of the desired course (see [Attachment 2])
- Information to submit: student ID / name / academic advisor / email address / mobile phone number

3. English Presentation Skills Seminar (details to be announced later)
- Date and place: Friday, 4 September 2026, 2:00–3:00 p.m., planned to be online (Zoom)
- Content: a lecture on English presentation skills.
- Note: participation is not mandatory for auditing students; only those who wish may apply (participation is recommended in the registration semester).

4. Important Notes
a. Courses with the same name other than the 16 courses in [Attachment 2] are recognised as general graduate courses, not the mandatory Master's/Doctoral Seminar (the subtitle code/subtitle name differ).
b. Because the first semester of the module Master's/Doctoral Seminar is conducted as auditing, take care not to formally register for the course during the course registration period.
c. You must apply to audit a course offered by the module you belong to (your academic advisor's module) (see [Attachment 2]).
 ※ For the Master's Seminar in the 'Semiconductor' and 'Computer' modules, you may apply to audit the course that corresponds to your presentation topic.

5. Inquiries: the department office (Building 301, Room 319). The contact details are in the original notice.

[Attachment 1] Fall 2026 Mandatory Graduate Master's/Doctoral Seminar 'Auditing' Guide (New Students)
[Attachment 2] Fall 2026 Module Master's/Doctoral Seminar Courses and Teaching Assistant List
